premeditation_planning: Yes, for the purpose of human sacrifice
key_evidence_accepted: Medical evidence substantiated the case of prosecution, parents of the deceased identified the cloths which the deceased child was wearing, and the FSL Report conclusively established that PW-3 was the biological relative of the deceased.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their evidence was strong, consistent, and corroborated by other evidence on record.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 04.03.2010, Trial judgment: 30.11.2016, High Court decision: 30.11.2016, Supreme Court decision: 03.10.2019
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Siddhartha Dave, Sumeer Sodhi, and others; Counsel for the State: Sumeer Sodhi and others
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and death sentence; High Court: Confirmed conviction, modified death sentence to life imprisonment; Supreme Court: Partly allowed the appeal, acquitted for offences under Sections 364/34 and 120B IPC, confirmed conviction and sentence for offences under Sections 302/34 and 201 IPC
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants were responsible for the gruesome murder of the children, as evidenced by the recovery of skeletal remains, confessions, and the identification of the cloths by the parents of the deceased. The medical evidence and independent witness testimonies corroborated the guilt of the accused.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, citing contradictions in the evidence, the possibility of planted evidence, and the lack of corroborative evidence for the confessional statements. They also raised doubts about the reliability of the DNA and forensic evidence.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle under Section 106 of the Evidence Act, placing the burden on the accused to explain how the body came to be buried in their house, and emphasized that the prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
precedent_relied_upon: Aghnoo Nagesia v. State of Bihar AIR 1966 SC 119; Ronny v. State of Maharashtra (1998) 3 SCC 625; Firozuddin Basheeruddin & Ors. v. State of Kerala (2001) 7 SCC 596; Shambu Nath Mehra v. The State of Ajmer [1956] SCR 199; Sahadevan & Anr. v. State of Tamil Nadu (2012) 6 SCC 403; State of Goa v. Sanjay Thakran (2007) 3 SCC 755; Prakash v. State of Karnataka (2014) 12 SCC 133
sentencing_rationale: The sentence was imposed due to the gruesome nature of the murder, and the High Court's modification to life imprisonment without remission or parole was confirmed by the Supreme Court.
